newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALGERIAN DRUGS FIRM LOSES $32 MLN.
newsitem.headline: ALGERIAN DRUGS FIRM LOSES $32 MLN.

text.p: Algeria's pharmaceutical products distribution company, Encopharm, posted a 1.8 billion dinars ($32 million) loss in 1996, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Monday.
State-owned Encopharm, based in the eastern city of Constantine, had a 13.493 billion ($240.9 million) turnover in 1996, said APS without giving comparative figures.
The cement and byproducts firm, Ciments et Derives de Chlef, made 121 million dinars ($2.16 million) profit in 1996, said APS.

The cement entreprise, based in the western town of Chlef, posted 8.04 billion dinars ($143.5 million) turnover, the agency added without saying what the results were for the previous year. ($1=56 dinars)
